chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Bureyd al-Ijli, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'There is a debt upon me,' and I think he said, 'For the orphans,' and I fear that if I sell my estate, I will remain with nothing. So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Do not sell your estate, but give some of it and withhold some.'
ai.seo_question: How should one pay off a debt without losing their primary property or estate?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practical dilemma of a debtor fearing destitution if forced to sell his primary asset. The Imam’s ruling to pay in installments while retaining the property highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-yusr* (ease) and preventing *al-ghurm* (loss), ensuring the debtor maintains a means of livelihood while fulfilling the obligation. This approach underscores the ethical imperative of preserving the debtor's dignity and economic stability, a key theme in Shia commercial jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Bureyd Al Ijaly who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that, ‘There are debts upon me’, and I think he (the narrator) said, ‘For the orphans, and I fear that if I were to sell my remaining place, there would be nothing left for me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not sell your place, but give some of it and withhold some’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Burayd al- ‘ Ij liy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I am indebted’ - I think he said, ‘to the orphans’ and I am afraid if I sell my property I will be left without any assets.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not sell your property; however, you should pay a certain part and keep certain other parts.’” (Fatwa best explains this Hadith)
